queries: WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) / AVG(HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) <> 0), a AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg1 FROM r), k1 AS (SELECT r.ID, r.ratio, r.ratio - a.avg1 AS above1 FROM r CROSS JOIN a WHERE r.ratio > a.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.ratio, k1.above1, k1.ratio - a2.avg2 AS above2 FROM k1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE k1.ratio > a2.avg2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(above1) AS avg_above_overall_avg, AVG(above2) AS avg_above_second_avg FROM k2

WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) <> 0), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m1 FROM r), k1 AS (SELECT r.ID, r.ratio, r.ratio - a1.m1 AS diff1 FROM r, a1 WHERE r.ratio > a1.m1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.ratio, k1.diff1, k1.ratio - a2.m2 AS diff2 FROM k1, a2 WHERE k1.ratio > a2.m2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(diff1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(diff2) AS avg_above_second FROM k2

WITH r AS (SELECT ID, ratio FROM (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID) WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL), k1 AS (SELECT ID, ratio, ratio - (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM r) AS d1 FROM r WHERE ratio > (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM r)), k2 AS (SELECT ID, ratio, d1, ratio - (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM k1) AS d2 FROM k1 WHERE ratio > (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM k1)) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_second FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: The 'average ratio across all patients' is the mean of the per-patient ratios (AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT) for each patient), not a pooled ratio of overall means.
Patients with no non-null HGB or no non-null HCT values (or an average HCT of 0) have no defined ratio and are excluded from all averages.
The second average is the mean ratio of the patients kept after the first filter, and the second filter is strictly above it.

responses.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(HCT) <> 0), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m1 FROM r), k1 AS (SELECT r.ID, r.ratio, r.ratio - a1.m1 AS diff1 FROM r, a1 WHERE r.ratio > a1.m1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS m2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.ratio, k1.diff1, k1.ratio - a2.m2 AS diff2 FROM k1, a2 WHERE k1.ratio > a2.m2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(diff1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(diff2) AS avg_above_second FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: The overall average ratio is the unweighted mean of the per-patient ratios. Only patients with a non-null, non-zero average HGB and HCT are included, because the others have no ratio.
The ratio is each patient's AVG(HGB) divided by their AVG(HCT), where each average covers that patient's non-null values across all their laboratory rows.
The comparison is strictly greater than at both filtering steps.

assumptions.assumption: The 'average ratio across all patients' is the mean of the per-patient ratios (AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT) per patient), not a pooled ratio over all lab rows.
Patients whose ratio cannot be computed (no non-null HGB or HCT, or average HCT of 0) are excluded from all averages.
Patients are grouped by Laboratory.ID, so only patients with lab records are considered.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average ratio is pooled across all lab rows: the overall average HGB divided by the overall average HCT, rather than the mean of per-patient ratios. The second average (of the kept group) is still the mean of the kept patients' ratios.
